title: Baltor Context Engine
tagline: Continuous reconciliation, anti-fragility, enhancement, optimization, and provenance

verification_rail.title: Continuous verification + adversarial validation
verification_rail.checks: contradictions  /  source precedence  /  fragile facts  /  missing evidence  /  freshness  /  policy risk
verification_rail.long: Prioritized continuous verification and adversarial interrogation runs below every stage, checking contradictions, source precedence, freshness windows, and policy.

stages.title: Source Systems
stages.copy: Captures organizational knowledge exactly where it lives, preserving timestamps, permissions, content hashes, and expandable source handles.

detail.subtitle: Raw context is preserved, not trusted
detail.copy: Example: Jira comments, Confluence pages, code, architecture diagrams, incidents, and local memory enter with timestamps, permissions, hashes, and source handles before any claim is trusted.

stages.title: Reconciliation
stages.copy: Deduplicates related artifacts, maps relationships, identifies comments-versus-decisions, and surfaces contradictions across tickets, docs, code, and memory.

detail.subtitle: Resolve disagreements across sources
detail.copy: Example: Jira says refunds are approved after 30 days, an old policy page says 14 days, and the billing service uses 21 days. Baltor links the evidence, chooses the highest-confidence source when policy allows, or flags the conflict for review.

stages.title: Anti-Fragility
stages.copy: Finds facts likely to change in source systems and replaces brittle text with robust knowledge objects that can update over time.

detail.subtitle: Replace brittle facts with robust knowledge objects
detail.copy: Example: magic numbers, settings, refund policies, thresholds, and limits are treated as volatile. Baltor creates refreshable objects and tools so the value can be rechecked against the right system instead of copied into stale context.

stages.title: Enhancement
stages.copy: Adds relevant external context objects, metadata, relationships, architecture/service graph links, event/schema facts, and missing connective context.

detail.subtitle: Augment with verified external context
detail.copy: Example: if internal sources disagree about the maximum allowable credit card late fee, Baltor can attach verified external sources or approved tools to resolve the conflict before the pack is served.

stages.title: Optimization
stages.copy: Summarizes, distills, converts unstructured context into structured objects, ranks relevance, and fits the result to the task budget.

detail.subtitle: Shape context into a compact task pack
detail.copy: Example: a 40-page policy thread, three tickets, and five source handles become a 3,000-token review pack: ranked claims, conflicts, tests to run, and expansion links. Benefit: less token waste, fewer tool calls, and less irrelevant context.

stages.title: Consumption
stages.copy: Serves task-specific packs to AI workflows and humans, allowing precise source-handle expansion while recording every pack claim, route, and decision.

detail.subtitle: Serve context with receipts and controlled expansion
detail.copy: Example: Claude, Cursor, another context layer, an internal workflow, or a human dashboard receives the same governed pack. Each consumer can expand approved source handles while Baltor records what was served, why, and under which policy.
